description: The NHERI SimCenter provides software for high-performance computational workflows, user support and educational material to advance the United States' ability to simulate the impact of natural hazards on structures, lifelines and communities. Its research applications address modelling, analysis and simulation across hazards and build in uncertainty quantification and optimisation: quoFEM combines finite element programs such as FEAPpv with UQ tools such as Dakota; EE-UQ computes a structure's response to earthquake excitation; Hydro-UQ assesses buildings under tsunami and storm surge loading by coupling 2D shallow-water results to a 3D CFD solver; WE-UQ assesses building performance under wind loading, now including component and cladding loads; and the PBE application performs performance-based engineering for buildings in earthquakes. The latest listed releases are quoFEM 4.2 and EE-UQ 4.2 (September 2025), Hydro-UQ 4.2 (August 2025) and WE-UQ 4.4 (September 2025). The site also hosts a teaching gallery, webinars, office hours and a software sharing plan for bringing research tools into the maintained ecosystem, and recently released a DLML Explorer for damage and loss model libraries. Coverage: generic. Access: downloadable apps with user manuals. Licence: WE-UQ is described as open source; each application carries its own licence. Caveats: the tools are research grade and need engineering expertise and, for large runs, DesignSafe computing. Simulation uses: building response and loss under earthquake, wind and surge for resilience studies. Related records: R2D, pelicun, OpenSees and the FEMA P-58 database.
